linkage_method: kill timestamp minus the attempt's measured wall must land within 5.0s of when the runtime wrote that attempt's request, and the runner-up candidate must be more than 30.0s away; two independently recorded clocks agreeing, not a label

registered_limits.defect: 2 workers x 4 GiB is an 8 GiB ceiling on a 9.72 GiB host that also runs the editor, the data collectors and other agent tools. The per-worker limit is enforced and measured; the host-level aggregate is neither

supersede_reason: the -01 record linked kills to attempts with a 1s window and no ambiguity check, so one of the two attempts was left unlinked on a 3.2s clock offset. The measurements are identical; the linkage rule is stricter, not the numbers
what_happened: both registered BTC control shards were SIGKILLed by the kernel OOM killer ~26 minutes into their first attempt; neither had reached its own registered 4 GiB worker limit
who_pushed_the_host_over: the kernel chose the lab workers at 11:10:52 and 11:12:31; the same ring buffer shows 'opencode' killed at 10:49:28, 12:00:01, 12:07:46 and 12:10:24 holding 2.29-3.04 GiB each time. A second agent tool on the same 9.72 GiB host is the proximate cause
